rounds.text: The market capitalization of Oscar Global Ltd sits at a micro-cap level of ₹ 7.13 Cr [E2], yet the business has demonstrated accelerating underlying earnings expansion that the headline numbers fail to capture fully. Compounded profit growth over the last three years has accelerated to 16% [E8], improving upon its five-year compounded profit growth rate of 13% [E7]. This consistent upward trajectory in profit growth proves that the operational engine is generating expanding returns over medium-term horizons. Furthermore, the stock is trading at the very top of its 52-week range at ₹ 21.6, capturing 100% of its yearly price span from a low of 10 [E4]. Conceded: [E3], [E5], and [E6].

The market capitalization of ₹ 7.13 Cr [E2] supports a business whose return on capital employed sits in negative territory at -3.8% [E5]. Furthermore, return on equity mirrors this destruction of value at -3.8% [E6], demonstrating that capital is actively eroding rather than compounding under current operations. Investors receive zero income protection for bearing these operational losses, as the dividend yield stands flat at 0.00% [E3]. Despite this fundamental wealth destruction, the stock trades at 2.48x book value on a price of ₹ 21.6 against a book value of ₹ 8.70 [E1], leaving it priced at the absolute ceiling of its 52-week range [E4]. Conceded: compounded profit growth reached 16% over 3 years [E8] and 13% over 5 years [E7].

Conceded: return on capital employed and return on equity are both at -3.8% [E5, E6]. However, focusing purely on these static efficiency ratios ignores the accelerating fundamental momentum demonstrated by a compounded profit growth of 16% over 3 years [E8], which outpaces the 13% rate achieved over the 5-year span [E7]. This acceleration proves that the underlying earning power of the business is actively strengthening despite the negative capital returns [E5, E6]. While the dividend yield is absent at 0.00% [E3], the retention of all earnings directly fuels this top-tier profit expansion. Furthermore, the market capitalization of ₹ 7.13 Cr [E2] and the 2.48x price-to-book valuation [E1] do not represent an unjustified ceiling just because the stock rests at the peak of its 52-week range [E4]; rather, it reflects a market beginning to properly price in this improving multi-year profit trajectory [E8].
